_meta.status: Step 2 ratified (V7, V8, V10, V11, V12, V13, V14); COMBAT.md debts discharged
provenance_notes: Stat leans, naming conventions, and dispositions are ratified canon (Q28); their numeric encodings here are proposed.
Age curves, pool_weights, market multipliers, loyalty bands, resentment rates, and every fossil_lexicon entry are (proposed) — veto freely.
Lean encoding: '++' → +3, '+' → +2, human 'mild' → +1, '−' → −2, '−−' → −3. Balancing offsets beyond RACES.md are flagged in 'lean_notes'.
The Ankoth are excluded by design (canon, Q24): banished non-playable lore race. Not omission.
pool_weights are relative fleet-wide base rates per recruitment pool; corp nattie pools multiply these by oa_profiles.json race_weights.
v0.2: the two COMBAT.md debts recorded in this file are discharged. mon_wa.special.tether_note and thythyn.special.wing_injury_table now point at the ratified model rather than owing it.

races.name: Human
races.absorption_note: Founders of the Opes Arx (pre-VC 08); arrived in the Crux as an outside diaspora, origins out of scope.
races.lore: Physically outmatched by every other fleet species; famous instead for will, versatility, and leadership gravity. They study broadly, change tactics when the situation demands it, and disproportionately end up in command.
races.lean_notes: Mild leans per RACES.md; widest trait variety and captain premium carried in 'special'.
races.resentment_note: Founders — the Spent Cradles are not theirs to mourn. Cradleborn Resentment does not roll on humans.

special.notes: captain_aptitude_bonus feeds captain fidelity (Step 4+); trait_variety_bonus widens general-pool trait draws.

naming.note: Earth-diaspora names drifted through fleet generations; cross-cultural blends common, occasionally corp-tinged for old company families (ratified).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: any solid ground underfoot — the old word for the lost home; muttered when boots hit planet
drop-bay farewell; nobody remembers the god
any disaster at all, not just the distress call it once was

races.name: Kellis
races.lore: Mantis-featured and precise; reputed the most honorable warriors in the Crux, treating the moment of battle as a dance. Loyal, trustworthy, and among the most sought-after recruits in the Divide.
races.lean_notes: ++aim / +reflex per RACES.md — lore precision maps onto the all-ranged canon.
races.pool_note: Rare in the Kier Bastille — honor culture (proposed).

special.ceremonial_blades: Cultural dueling arts hone marksman's discipline; blades are never fielded (canon). Cosmetic kit + broadcast color only.
special.notes: pact_reputation: kellis-heavy squads strengthen pact-keeping credibility (negotiation hook, Step 6).

naming.note: Two soft measured words, given + family, ~2 syllables each, open vowels, consonants from k/t/l/sh/n/s/r (ratified; canon anchor: Kintu Elesh).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: the stillness before the dance begins; said to a squadmate, it means good luck
grace under fire — the compliment paid to a clean shot
a debt of honor that outlives the debtor

races.name: Mon-Wa
races.lore: Pet-like in appearance and vastly more useful than they look: each Mon-Wa is a pair of telepathically linked symbiotes — one being in two bodies. Gentle, clever, resourceful; among the least hostile species in the fleet and among the most sought-after recruits.
races.lean_notes: +fieldcraft/+tactics per RACES.md; the aim/grit offsets encode 'modest combat output for two bodies' (proposed).
races.pool_note: Rare in the Bastille — least hostile species in the fleet (proposed).

market.rarity_note: One salary line buys two bodies; priced for the utility, not the firepower.

special.tether_note: Canon: cannot be split-tasked beyond miles; forced separation risks collapse. MODEL DELIVERED (COMBAT.md 8.1): day-loop tether enforced at squad assignment; in-engagement the halves must share an engagement and adjacent bands, and separation costs -25 composure/exchange to both plus aim_eff -4.
special.partner_death_note: Canon outcomes common/uncommon/rare; numbers ratified V13. Roll fires immediately mid-engagement; a traumatized survivor is auto-downed for the remainder, takes scar traits, and is renamed (Em- prefix for a widowed Mon, -Em suffix for a widowed Wa).
special.notes: Disproportionate value in camp, logistics, and intel roles (ratified).
special.combat_model: Two bodies, two shots, ONE composure pool, ONE shared wound track: a serious wound to either body downs the pair (COMBAT.md 8.1, C14a ratified).

naming.note: Each half named separately, 3–4 letters, addressed together as {Mon}-{Wa}. Widowed Mon takes Em- prefix; widowed Wa takes -Em suffix (ratified; canon anchors: Bahn-Kal, Ari-Onn, Em-Mak).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: severed; alone — the language's saddest word (surviving grammar: the widow particle, canon)
the felt hum of a healthy bond; contentment
any bonded pair — extended, as an honor, to trusted squadmates

races.name: Olmac
races.lore: Towering forces of nature with leathery, granite-colored flesh — outsized only by the banished Ankoth. What they lack in cunning they repay in overwhelming battlefield skill, smothering enemies in firepower. No true loyalty: they take any role that puts them on a battlefield.
races.lean_notes: ++grit / −tactics / −fieldcraft per RACES.md ('nothing that size hides' pushed fieldcraft to −3); the aim/resolve nudges encode smothering fire and unsentimental steadiness (proposed).
races.pool_note: Demographic ubiquity is canon: present in every corp's pools and the merc market.

market.rarity_note: Cheap to sign, easy to lose (canon).

special.media_note: Barely speaks — spends words like they cost blood (canon language ruling). Media statements flat; broadcast novelty when one DOES speak.
special.armor_ruling: The concept art's sealed gold armor is one individual's kit, not racial physiology (canon ruling).

naming.note: Titles, not names: the definite article + a single evocative noun or adjective (ratified; canon anchors: The Grin, The Pillar, The Heart, The Tame).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: assent — as much conversation as most Olmac offer
enough; stop — also their only word for death

races.name: Thythyn
races.lore: Moth-like, agile, intelligent — the fleet's only fliers, and skilled at every range of a fight. Between Divides many work as mercenaries; they excel under orders and under pressure, and they are intensely status-focused, always maneuvering up the chain.
races.lean_notes: +reflex/+aim/+fieldcraft per RACES.md; the grit offset encodes light frames and fragile wings (proposed).

age.provenance: proposed — short bright careers feed the status urgency

races.loyalty_texture_note: Canon: morale and loyalty track fame, rank, and captaincy prospects; a passed-over Thythyn sours.
races.oa_lean_note: Historically spread evenly; Alliance House numbers rising (canon).

special.range_note: 'Equally skilled at all ranges' renders as no range-band penalties in the all-ranged canon (ratified).
special.wing_injury_table: DELIVERED (COMBAT.md 7.2): inj_wing_tear 01-40 minor / inj_wing_strut 41-72 serious, grounded for the Divide / inj_wing_spar 73-92 critical / inj_wing_loss 93-00 permanent. Substituted for general-table rolls 01-36; brittle_wings widens to 01-48, updraft_ace narrows to 01-28.
special.flight_note: NOT a flying unit (C14b ratified). Wings buy fast reposition (two exchanges become one) and a brief hover: one exchange of elevated firing that ignores one step of the target's cover at motion_mult 1.35 against themselves. Rigs and updraft_ace reduce that exposure.

naming.note: Given: one airy vowel-starved y-heavy syllable. Family: two syllables with a doubled consonant (ratified; canon anchor: Lyv Kallik).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: an updraft; any opening worth taking
a superior worth following — from a Thythyn, high praise
a bad landing; disgrace

races.name: Svalbard
races.cohabitant_note: Unknowing cohabitants of Kranoia beside the Ankoth (banished).
races.lore: Imposing feline figures — massive upper bodies carried on four legs. Known for wisdom, long tradition, and training years that include the killing of their own young; the surviving adults are elite hybrids of speed, strength, and intellect, famous for long military careers.
races.lean_notes: Strong across grit/reflex/tactics/presence with high floors (ratified) — the culls mean weak Svalbard mostly don't exist.

age.provenance: long primes are canon-vibe; numbers proposed

races.pool_note: The pool skews elite, rare, and expensive (ratified).

special.tradition_note: Resistant to doctrine changes and mid-Divide policy whiplash — they signed for a banner, not a mood (ratified).
special.notes: Whispered about as a cause of the fleet's slow decline (lore).

naming.note: Melodic given names of 2–3 syllables with a classical ring + short hard pride names, shared and heavy with tradition (ratified; canon anchors: Alyrion Vonn, Lanthas Vonn, Armas Jannik).
naming.pride_note: Prides are a finite list on purpose — repeats across fighters are kin, not collisions.

fossil_lexicon.gloss: the pride's unbroken line; spoken as a toast
an unculled cub — a stinging insult to any adult
a winter endured; hard times survived

races.name: Etu
races.lore: Reptilian, tough, endlessly adaptive — and the fleet's mystics. Nearly all Etu follow Et-y-Bellum, the faith that their people were made as instruments of battle: healing, scouting, or pulling the trigger, every role is worship, and battle is the spectacle their lives were purposed for.
races.lean_notes: +grit/+fieldcraft/+resolve per RACES.md (faith under fire); the presence offset encodes stoicism (proposed).
races.supply_note: Cold-blooded low metabolism → reduced field supply consumption (canon management hook).

special.devotion_note: Nearly all Etu hold the faith; the traits mark the visibly devout and the zealous. Zealots and war-priests take the Et- honorific prefix (ratified).
special.cede_friction: Devout Etu take loyalty/morale hits when their corp cedes — the sacrament abandoned (ratified, spicier variant).

naming.note: Mononyms, 1–2 syllables, hard consonants, mandatory doubled letter — vowel or consonant. Et- honorific for clergy and zealots (ratified; canon anchors: Stokk, Koruuth, Mazzk, Oort, Gurrim).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: battle as sacrament — from Et-y-Bellum, the surviving phrase
a made thing; an instrument — also the honorific particle for the devout
a wasted death — dying far from battle; their bitterest word

races.name: Attorak
races.lore: Gnoll-like and fierce, discovered mid-war against the Gil for the water planet Keshu; the Opes Arx brokered the peace and embraced both. Attorak thrive in combat, flock to the Nevlon Collective's militarist creed, and are heavily credited whenever Nevlon's dominance is discussed.
races.lean_notes: +grit/+resolve per RACES.md (fearless in the fight); the presence nudge encodes crowd-legible savagery (proposed).
races.pool_note: Overrepresented in the Bastille — battle-joy finds trouble between Divides (proposed).
races.resentment_note: Keshu died recently, as cradles go — the memory is fresh (proposed recency weighting).

special.language_note: Their grasp of English stays loose (canon) — broadcast color, mangled idioms, subtitle jokes.
special.mimicry: Named for vocal mimics produced in their youth (canon) — comms/decoy utility surfaces as a trait.

naming.note: A sound from their youth they associate with themselves and verbalize constantly: mangled sound-effect words, 1–2 percussive syllables, reduplication welcome (canon convention; anchors: Bonq, Hikkup, Boum).

fossil_lexicon.gloss: an excited yes — barked, often several times
disappointment; a fight called off
water — and grief; both, ever since Keshu

races.name: Gil
races.lore: Short-statured, blue-skinned, trunk-horned — and nearly blind, famous for the goggles that give them back the world. Magnificently agile masters of ambush who held their own against the Attorak through the War for Keshu. Culturally individualist: each Gil enlists wherever best serves their own goals. Some are born psionic.
races.lean_notes: ++fieldcraft / ++reflex per RACES.md; the grit offset encodes small frames (proposed).
races.loyalty_texture_note: Canon: they stay while you serve their goals.
races.pool_note: Bastille lean: patient hunters get caught holding other people's property (proposed).
races.resentment_note: Keshu recency, as with the Attorak (proposed).

special.vision: Racially impaired vision — goggles are corrective equipment on every Gil, not kit (canon ruling). Optional damaged-goggles quirk lands with COMBAT.md gear rules.

psionics.note: Scope defined here per RACES.md: rare trait line, one expression per psion. Rates proposed.

naming.note: Long exuberant Latinate given (4–5 syllables, -us/-ius) shortened to a 3-letter nickname + short family-house name; houses repeat (ratified; canon anchors: Elioysus (Eli) Bentu, Uriosirus (Uri) Bentu, Onimirius (Oni) Fynn, Anamagdrius (Ana) Tahl).
naming.house_note: Finite house list on purpose — Bentu repeats in canon; family houses ratified with the v0.1 sheet.

fossil_lexicon.gloss: the world seen clearly; truth — what the goggles restore
the perfect moment to strike; whispered, never shouted
a favor owed — the true currency of Gil society
